title: Recorded-response integration tests
scope: tests/integration/ drives the module through a server on 127.0.0.1. Catalog, quote and challenge bodies come from the sandbox recording. Sign-in tokens, one completed-detail probe, and the login, missing-token and unknown-token bodies built by the server do not. Expired-detail and failed-widget-login bodies are returned by the test fetch, not by that server.

entries.status: fake — recorded sandbox responses played by a local server
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] loads tests/integration/fixtures/sandbox.json. [ref 1] is the recording time in that file. [ref 2] listens on 127.0.0.1. [ref 3] rejects a request that is not in the recording.
entries.insteadOf: the live DFX API as it answers today
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that the live DFX API still returns these bodies.

anchor: if (!entry) throw new Error(`Unrecorded DFX request: ${request.method} ${request.url} body=${body}`)

entries.component: DFX access token and completed transaction detail
entries.status: fake — synthesized by the replay server
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] answers a successful login with a local access token, not a body from the recording. [ref 1] answers the completedDetail fault with a fixed Buy body in state Completed.
entries.insteadOf: an access token issued by the DFX API, and a transaction detail read from that API

entries.status: fake — synthesized by the replay server
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] answers a rejected login with a local 401 or 400 body. [ref 1] answers the missing-token fault with HTTP 201 and an empty object, and the comment marks that response as not a recorded success. [ref 2] answers an unknown detail token with a local 401. This server does not build the expired-detail or failed-widget-login responses. The tests return those.
entries.insteadOf: error bodies returned by the live DFX API
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that the live DFX API returns these error bodies.

entries.status: fake — the test fetch returns HTTP 401
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] waits until two detail requests present the first bearer token, then returns HTTP 401 and { message: 'Expired detail session' } instead of the replay response. [ref 1] returns that same status and body for a detail request whose bearer token is the one the test has marked rejected, after optionally waiting for the test to release it. [ref 2] only records each request and then forwards it to the replay server, or to the fetch the test passed in. [ref 3] forwards the replay response and, for one detail call, waits before returning that same response. [ref 2] and [ref 3] are not stand-ins.
entries.insteadOf: an HTTP 401 from the DFX API for an expired session
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that the DFX API reports an expired session with this body.

entries.status: fake — the test fetch returns HTTP 401
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] returns HTTP 401 and { message: 'Widget login failed' } for the second POST /v1/auth. It also reads each auth response, cloning it when the response has clone, and records the status and parsed body; the recorded copy is not what the module receives. [ref 1] returns that same status and body for the second POST /v1/auth when the case asks the login to fail. Otherwise [ref 1] counts the login and forwards the request to the replay server, which is not a stand-in.
entries.insteadOf: an HTTP 401 from the DFX API for a rejected widget login
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that the DFX API rejects a widget login with this body.

entries.component: Smart account and its first signature
entries.mechanism: [ref 0] is not an ERC-4337 account or a Safe. getAddress returns the address passed to the constructor, or 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001, and sign and signTypedData record the payload and then call the inner account. [ref 1] returns the signature given to its constructor on the first sign call, and only a later sign call uses the inner account. The unit record entry Signing account does not cover DummySmartAccount or DummyFirstSignature.
entries.insteadOf: a smart account, ERC-4337 or Safe, and the signature of its first authentication
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that a smart account signs in or that its first signature is accepted.
